solution_full: The summation set is all pairs with $0\le i<j\le6$. Fix $j$ and sum over $i=0,1,\dots,j-1$ first.
$\displaystyle\sum_{i=0}^{j-1}\binom{j}{i}=\sum_{i=0}^{j}\binom{j}{i}-\binom{j}{j}=2^{j}-1$ (for $j=0$ the inner sum is empty and $2^{0}-1=0$ agrees).
(Counting interpretation: choose a subset $J$ of $\{1,\dots,6\}$ and a subset of $J$ of smaller size: $3^{6}$ nested pairs minus the $2^{6}$ with equality.)
originality_note: New: a nested double sum C(6,j) C(j,i) over i < j, summed inner-first to 2^j - 1 and then by the binomial theorem twice (way 5). Closest known: sum C(n,j) C(j,i) over all i <= j = 3^n. Different because: the strict inequality removes the diagonal and gives 3^n - 2^n.

concept_use.Double Summations in Binomial Coefficien: The double sum over 0 <= i < j <= 6 is evaluated inner-first (2^j - 1) and then outer by the binomial theorem.

stem_review: Read as a student: the summation set 0 <= i < j <= 6 is explicit; answer 665 is a positive 3-digit integer as planned; Hindi mirrors. No change.
key_step: Sum over i first to get 2^j - 1.
justification: Two applications of the binomial theorem after reordering the double sum; routine multi-step. Comparable to 2021-P2-Q1 (L2).
